newsitem.title: CHINA: Earthquake rocks southwest China, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks southwest China, no casualties.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.1 on the Richter scale rocked southwest China on Saturday, but there were no immediate reports of casualties, officials said.
The earthquake hit Jinghong city in Yunnan province at 10:38 a.m. (0238 GMT), but did not cause any casualties or damages, a seismological official told Reuters by telephone.
Local officials in neighbouring Mengla and Menghai counties also reported no deaths or injuries.
Some houses in Mengla county were slightly damaged, the officials said. The tallest building in the area has four floors.
The area rocked by the earthquake is near the border with Burma and Laos. It is thinly populated and inhabited mainly by farmers who are members of the Dai minority group.
In the northwestern region of Xinjiang, authorities on Friday began evacuating people from houses considered unsafe, the Xinhua news agency said.
Residents were moved after seismologists warned that there could be a number of aftershocks measuring more than five on the open-ended Richter scale, Xinhua said.
The mainly Moslem region of sheep herders and cotton farmers was hit by an earthquake measuring 6.4 on the Richter scale on Tuesday, followed one minute later by a tremor measuring 6.3.
State television has said nearly 50 people were killed, but Xinhua put the toll at 12 dead and 40 injured.

The two earthquakes destroyed 14,000 houses and seriously damaged 1,700, leaving thousands of families homeless and living in tents in freezing temperatures, state television has said. Officials say about 20,000 houses were damaged.
Meanwhile, soldiers arrived in the disaster area of Jiashi near the bazaar town of Kashgar to help with rescue and relief work, and army doctors treated the injured, reports said.
The People's Liberation Army had donated clothing and transported more than 100 tonnes of relief materials to the quake-stricken areas, they said.
An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude rocked Jiashi in Xinjiang last March, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
